# γ-H2AX

**γ-H2AX** is the phosphorylated form of the histone variant [[Histone H2A.Z|H2AX]] at serine 139 (Ser139), generated by [[ATM]], [[ATR]], and [[DNA-PK]] kinases in response to [[DNA Damage|DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs)]]. It is the canonical and most widely used molecular marker for DSB detection and repair kinetics.

## Mechanism

Within minutes of DSB formation, hundreds to thousands of H2AX molecules flanking the break site are phosphorylated to form distinct nuclear foci (γ-H2AX foci). These foci serve as a recruitment platform for [[DNA Repair]] proteins, including [[53BP1]], [[BRCA1]], and [[MDC1]], amplifying the DNA damage signal and facilitating [[Homologous Recombination|homologous recombination]] or [[Non-Homologous End Joining|non-homologous end joining]].

## Role in Sirtuin Biology

[[SIRT6]] promotes DSB repair by deacetylating H3K9ac and H3K56ac, which facilitates [[53BP1]] and [[BRCA1]] recruitment to damage sites. γ-H2AX foci clearance kinetics is the standard functional readout for SIRT6-dependent DNA repair efficiency. Accelerated γ-H2AX resolution upon [[SIRT6]] activation (via [[UBCS039]] or [[MDL-800]]) directly demonstrates enhanced DSB repair capacity.

## Applications

- **DNA Repair Assays**: Quantification of γ-H2AX foci by [[Immunofluorescence|immunofluorescence]] or flow cytometry pre- and post-irradiation measures repair kinetics.
- **Senescence & Aging**: Persistent γ-H2AX foci are a hallmark of [[Cellular Senescence|senescent cells]] and accumulate with age, reflecting genomic instability.
- **Drug Development**: Used as a pharmacodynamic biomarker for [[SIRT6]] activators, [[PARP inhibitors]], [[CDK inhibitors]], and [[Radiosensitizer|radiosensitizing agents]].

## Connections

- [[Histone H2A.Z]] — parent histone variant
- [[SIRT6]] — promotes repair, accelerating γ-H2AX clearance
- [[53BP1]] — co-localizes at DSB sites; commonly co-assayed
- [[DNA Repair]] — broader process for which γ-H2AX is the key marker
- [[DNA Damage]] — trigger for H2AX phosphorylation
- [[Cellular Senescence]] — persistent γ-H2AX foci as hallmark
